Inbox revamp, inspiration board

The inbox becomes one physical surface that moves like an app: things arrive, stack, fan open, get swiped away, and grow into the thread you tap. Nothing is a static box any more. Every move below is taken from a named 21st.dev reference whose source sits in 01-refs/source/; the skin (colours, radii, fonts) is ours, the MOVE is theirs. Canon stays: dark ground, pistachio frame, lime as the one accent, no serif.

01 Feed

Pool built: 283 candidates. Previews looked at: 30.

  1. 1Two densities in one list (Activity Feed, felipemenezes098): system events are one quiet line with a mono time; human events (a reply, a comment, a booking) get the full card with the quote. The feed stops looking like a wall of equal boxes.
  2. 2Actor · verb · object headline with the payload quoted inset and the one action inline on the row (Notifications Menu, ahmedmayara, 152 uses).
  3. 3Sticky day headers, the title and live count condense into a compact bar on scroll (Notification Scroll Area, bundui; Sticky Header, ddoemonn).
  4. 4A running row wears its state as motion: a soft wash sweeps under a mono state label while a lane is working, and settles flat when it stops (Card Status List, isaiahbjork, 71).
  5. 5New items land at the top with a stagger; a floating “3 new” pill appears only when something arrives while you are scrolled down and jumps you to it (Animated List, dillionverma, 298; New Items Pill, ddoemonn).
Interactive Logs Table moumensoliman · usage 153

move Every row is one fixed instrument grid, severity chip, monospace timestamp, source, message, right-aligned result code and duration, with a chevron that opens the detail in place.

in the inbox: Replaces the free-form card body. “Failed · Gemma Telford” becomes “[FAIL] 00:13 warm-drafter · couldn't write a reply · 502”. Ivan scans the edges of the column and never reads the middle unless he taps.

risk It is a desktop table. At 390px the five columns must fold to two lines, or it becomes a horizontally scrolling log viewer and dies.

03 Dismiss

Pool built: 90 candidates. Previews looked at: 14. Thinnest surface in the corpus.

  1. 8Swipe reveals the action under the card, the card resolves in place (a tick draws) before it leaves, the rows below settle with a spring, one undo toast (Todo List Item, uiverse; Swipe Row, molecule-lab-rushil; BeUI Swipeable List).
Todo List Item serafimcloud · usage 42

move The swipe reveals the action rather than performing it, and the row then RESOLVES IN PLACE, a strike-through animates across the text, before the row leaves.

in the inbox: Dismissing a card strikes it, dims it, holds for a beat, then collapses the row. Ivan sees which card he just killed, which is exactly what the current instant-delete denies him.

risk Port the timing and the resolve-then-leave sequence, none of the look. Hold the beat too long and the feed feels sluggish at ten dismisses a day.

demo video →
Collapsible Banner ddoemonn · usage 0

in the inbox: Gives Ivan the move he actually wants ten times a day: quiet this down without losing it. A read error folds to one line instead of vanishing.

risk A third state needs somewhere to live in the data model or folded cards resurrect on the next poll. A stub row that never clears is just clutter with extra steps.
